strengths: The focus on compact models for ten Indian languages is relevant to multilingual NLP and deployment with limited compute. Coverage includes languages that receive relatively little attention in generative modeling.
The work reports substantial corpus curation and model development, including 5,000 manually created Bangla instructions and culturally grounded generation prompts.

The reported instruction-tuning gains are promising: Belebele accuracy increases from 25.11 to 32.45 for Bangla and from 23.33 to 42.78 for Hindi. These results suggest value in further developing the compact models.
weaknesses: The proposed RoPE memory-saving contribution is not established. Rescaling positional indices alone does not reduce the attention and activation storage required to process longer sequences. The manuscript provides neither a sufficiently specified implementation nor controlled memory measurements. Comparing these small models trained on one GPU with LLaMA trained on thousands of GPUs does not isolate a context-length efficiency improvement.

Reproducibility is inadequate for Findings. Essential architecture dimensions, optimizer settings, learning-rate schedules, batch sizes, training steps, vocabulary sizes, and the exact BPE/Unigram combination procedure are missing. Corpus sources, per-language mixtures, and split construction are insufficiently documented, and no accessible model/code/tokenizer release is identified. CPU throughput also lacks hardware and measurement details.

The benchmark interpretation overstates the evidence for cross-lingual transfer. For example, mParamanu obtains 24.84 on MMLU-Hindi, 25.68 on MMLU-Marathi, and 49.24 on XStoryCloze-Hindi, against approximately 25%, 25%, and 50% chance performance. Such results cannot establish effective transfer. Confidence intervals and controlled comparisons are needed, particularly when claimed advantages are small. Several base models also underperform the multilingual baselines.

The human evaluation cannot support broad generative-superiority claims: it uses only four prompts per language and nominally three completions per prompt. Annotator allocation, blinding, agreement, and uncertainty are not reported. Factuality conflates unverifiable content with false content. The October 2023 ChatGPT website comparison does not establish matched decoding conditions, and comparisons against predominantly English models provide limited evidence of superiority over capable multilingual systems.

The tokenizer and multilingual-training explanations lack isolating experiments. Fertility comparisons do not document a common evaluation corpus and vocabulary-budget controls. Table 3 compares perplexities across languages and tokenizers, although these use different prediction units; the Konkani–Maithili perplexity comparison therefore does not establish better modeling by itself. Matched ablations are needed to distinguish effects of tokenization, corpus balance, language grouping, and training volume.

Reporting inconsistencies require an audit. Table 7's Hindi instruction-tuned scores average 38.49, not 40.14. Instruction-tuning data are variously described as 23,000 examples and 27,000 plus 52,000 Alpaca examples. Tables 12 and 19 attribute identical Bangla completions to different model sizes, and Tables 27–28 repeat some outputs under different baseline labels. These issues directly weaken confidence in the empirical evidence. Resolving them alongside the missing methodological validation requires substantial work before a sound Findings recommendation is possible.
